newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank sees Sweden meeting EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank sees Sweden meeting EMU criteria.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Wednesday it expected Sweden to meet the European Union's economic and monetary union inflation criteria this year.
Deputy Governor Stefan Ingves told a meeting it looked as though Sweden would, in general, meet all convergence criteria.
Ingves, reinforcing the central bank's support of a prompt Swedish EMU entry, said there was risk of discrimination by financial markets against countries that opted not to join EMU.
He said a wider debate was needed on the membership issue in Sweden, where popular opinion is broadly against EMU membership.
He called for preparations for Sweden to join EMU to proceed independently of political debate on the issue.
"Independently of the political debate, practical preparations must continue," he said, adding the Riksbank would publish a new report on EMU preparations in the autumn.
"For the moment, Sweden has the lowest inflation in Europe, and we expect that Sweden will fulfill the criteria concerning inflation in 1997. We will also probably fulfill the interest rate criteria.
"All things being equal, the situation looks as though we will, in fact, fulfill the convergence criteria," he added.

"We have witnessed concern in the financial sector over increased costs, falling competitiveness and risks of various forms of discrimination if we stay outside EMU," said Ingves, adding the Riksbank had asked 50 Swedish organisations it does not usally cooperate with to contribute their views to the debate.

Ingves said Sweden was still trying to decide whether to join EMU from January 1, 1999 or wait. "My hope is that we will, in the future, have a broader debate on this very important decision." -- Simon Haydon, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1004
